purpose: Characterise, by measurement, the difference between the agent sandbox's execution boundary and the real Windows host runtime, and record which gates that difference blocks.

section_1_delete_matrix_remeasured.conclusion: Unchanged from the earlier measurement. Denial is at the Win32 API layer, not ACLs -- `cmd.exe del` on the same path succeeds, so an ACL denial is excluded.

section_2_warmed_wal_write_DOES_work.why_measured: Distinguishes 'the sandbox cannot do SQLite at all' (false) from 'the sandbox cannot CREATE a database' (true).
section_2_warmed_wal_write_DOES_work.conclusion: Writing to an ALREADY-EXISTING WAL database succeeds and is durable. The fresh-DB failure is specifically the journal unlink performed while establishing the journal, not SQLite as such.

section_3_sandbox_descendants_are_reaped.why_measured: Determines whether any long-lived server started from the sandbox can be used for a multi-call gate.
section_3_sandbox_descendants_are_reaped.conclusion: The child was alive inside the call and dead 30 s later, having written nothing further. The per-call reaper is real and unavoidable, and it applies to the product's own launcher: scripts\jcc-v1.3.ps1 -Action up starts a detached child that is gone by the next tool call, which is why its 90 s health probe reported failure.

section_4_host_execution_lane_and_owners.conclusion: DURABLE_RUNTIME for the API half is VERIFIED through the product's own ownership contract: start(task) -> healthy -> official stop -> down -> official start -> recovered (new pid) -> mark -> status: ownership verified, with GREEN 4778 asserted untouched around every step. The UI half has no durable lane on this host.

section_5_a_sandboxed_api_binds_the_port.why_measured: The W10 perf harness booted its own product API on the warmed databases and then never became ready. This is the reason.
section_5_a_sandboxed_api_binds_the_port.conclusion: A sandboxed product API binds its socket and is reachable, but its request path is effectively unusable: the first DB write of a request stalls on the refused journal unlink, so a request either takes tens of seconds or is reset. This -- not the fresh-DB issue alone -- is what the earlier 90 s health-probe timeout was reporting.
